This Guidebook has been compiled as a single, comprehensive training and reference resource for the Mortgage Processing team, drawing together pre-approval procedures, valuation and inspection protocols, Final Offer Letter and loan booking workflows, final transfer and disbursal procedures, digital systems governance, and the full set of supporting matrices, checklists, bank-specific formats, fee structures, and directories used across the organization.
Readers should note that this document is, by its nature, a living record built up over time from multiple internal sources, presentations, checklists, and bank communications. As a result:

Some information — including certain policy figures, rates, fee amounts, portal links, and procedural steps — may reflect the position at the time it was originally recorded and may have since been revised by the respective banks or regulatory authorities.

Some staff names, designations, Relationship Manager (RM) allocations, and contact details mentioned throughout this Guidebook may change over time as personnel move roles, teams are restructured, or banks reassign their relationship managers.
Some procedures, portal names, submission channels (e.g., Huspy, Prypco, Direct), and internal workflows may be updated, replaced, or streamlined as the organization's processes evolve.

Nothing in this Guidebook has been deleted, shortened, or removed in the course of compiling this edition — every detail, matrix, checklist, template, and reference from the source materials has been retained in full so that no operational knowledge is lost.

As readers and users of this Guidebook become actively involved in day-to-day processing work, they are encouraged — and expected — to flag outdated names, rates, procedures, or contacts to their Team Leads so that this document can be reviewed and updated accordingly. This Guidebook should therefore be treated as a continuously evolving working document, to be corrected, refined, and kept current as the team's real-world experience grows, rather than a static, one-time publication. Updates, corrections, and version notes should be logged and circulated so that every team member always works from the most accurate available version.

Objective: To provide a standardized, step-by-step operational procedure for processing mortgage applications from initial document collection to the final property transfer, loan booking, disbursal, and post-completion quality checks. This document serves as the ultimate operational reference for all processing executives, ensuring compliance, accuracy, and maximum efficiency.

1. One Case, One Controlled Journey: A mortgage file is treated as a controlled case moving through defined stages. At every stage, the responsible person must know what has been received, verified, what remains outstanding, and who owns the next action.

2. Verification Before Submission: Never forward an incomplete document package. Verify client information against KYC and bank forms. Record and resolve discrepancies before treating the file as submission-ready.

3. Transaction Type Drives the Document Set: The required property documents change depending on whether the case is Primary, Resale, Buyout, or Equity. Identify the transaction type before building the file.
4. Stage Handover is a Control Point: A case moves to the next stage ONLY after the required handover items are available and checked.

Written Communication Only: All operational updates, bank queries, client confirmations, and stage handovers must be executed via email or logged system notes. Verbal communication is not treated as binding — keep all conversations through email only.

Rigid Maker-Checker Separation: Virtue Relationship Managers (VRMs) act as "Makers" — sourcing clients and gathering initial documentation. Sales Progression Officers (SPOs) act as "Checkers" — auditing, verifying, and submitting to banks. See Section 1.
4:30 PM Daily Bank-Submission Cutoff: File submission to the bank is targeted for the same day, with a 4:30 PM UAE time deadline for that day's batch.
Clean Drive Protocol: Temporary G-Drive folders must be purged daily upon task completion, and no created folders should remain in the shared drive before logging off. See Section 7.

Quality Benchmark — Max 4 Recalls per Month: Exceeding four file recalls in a month, providing wrong updates, or bypassing checklists triggers a formal Warning Letter; a third Warning Letter results in termination. See Section 1.5.

Before submitting to the bank, SPT must ensure the client meets basic eligibility criteria using internal calculators.
When greeting a customer, follow this strict 3-stage process:
Stage 1: Cash Requirement
1. Greet Customer.
2. Ask if it is their 1st property finance or an existing property finance in UAE, and determine their nationality.
3. Ask the property value.
4. Calculate cash needed in hand as per the required LTV using the website calculator. If the client asks for a breakup, provide it directly from the website calculator.
Stage 2: Installment Calculation
1. Go to the ROI sheet. Input the property value and bank rate of 2.69% (for Expats at 80% LTV). Note: For every customer, the initial calculation is based on 2.69%.
2. Get two confirmations: How much cash they have on hand, and provide the EMI breakup.
3. Inform them that a consultant will explain further details.
Stage 3: Age Calculator
1. Maximum tenure eligibility is 300 months (25 years).
2. Ask for the client's age and calculate using the age calculator.
3. Rule: If the current month on the calculator is, for example, September, change it to November (advance by one month).
4. Based on age, calculate and let the customer know their age eligibility, EMI, and cash needed. Inform them a consultant will call for a detailed discussion.

blocks.t: DIB Exception (Expats): Age increased to 70 years subject to ALL conditions: Length of service at least 2 years in UAE, Salary >= AED 40,000/month, and age at application is 50 years. Based on 70% LTV policy, eligible for 70 years tenor.
Maximum Tenor: 300 months (25 years) across the board.
GCC Nationals Rule: Customers from UAE, Oman, Kuwait, Bahrain, Saudi, and Qatar do not have visas and Emirates IDs. UAE Nationals only have a Family Book.
What is EIBOR? Emirates Inter Bank Offered Rate. Published by the UAE Central Bank on their website (https://www.centralbank.ae/en/forex-eibor/eibor-rates/).
Update Timing: Central Bank revises and updates rates daily, usually by 12:30 PM UAE Time.
Tenors Available: Day, Week, 1 Month, 3 Months, 6 Months, 1 Year.

Calculation Logic: If a bank uses a 1-Month EIBOR, they track the daily EIBOR for the whole month, sum it, and divide by the days of the month. This average becomes the EIBOR for the next month. For 3-Month EIBOR, the average of Jan-Mar dictates the rate for Apr-Jun. "Past is the EIBOR for the Future."
Impact on Client: If the client is on a floating/variable rate and EIBOR drops for 3 months, their interest will decrease in the next quarter.
Must strictly be below 50% in both actual and qualifying rates. If DSR goes above 50%, the CRM must trigger a pop-up or notification.
Formula: DBR = (Total Monthly Obligations / Monthly Income) x 100
Step-by-Step Calculation Logic & Example:
1. Determine Maximum Obligations: Monthly Salary (AED 20,000) x 50% = AED 10,000 Max DBR.
2. Sum Existing Liabilities: Car Loan (AED 2,000) + Personal Loan (AED 1,500) + Credit Card Min (AED 500) = AED 4,000 Total Liability.
3. Calculate Available Mortgage EMI: Max DBR (AED 10,000) - Total Liability (AED 4,000) = AED 6,000 available for mortgage installment.

Credit Card Liability Calculation: Even if the customer pays cards in full, banks calculate liability. Most banks use 5% of the Credit Card Limit. (e.g., Limit AED 50,000 x 5% = AED 2,500 monthly obligation).
RAK Bank Policy: 5% of the credit limit is considered for DBR calculations.
Liabilities Included: Existing loan installments, monthly rental income (if applicable), 5% of total credit card limits across all banks, monthly insurance premiums, monthly property insurance.

Income Considerations: Bonus (Arab Bank considers up to 50%), Incentives/Commission (Arab Bank up to 90% capped to monthly income). CBD does not consider bonus as part of income calculation. Rental income considered up to 70% of annual rental (Arab Bank caps at 25% of primary income). Rental income outside UAE cannot be considered (RAK Bank rule).

blocks.t: Meeting Reference: As per the meeting held on 13th August 2026 with Swathi, the VRM Team, the SPO Team, and Janardhan, the following new operational requirement is now in effect and must be strictly followed by all team members handling the Valuation Stage:

New Requirement: Once the property Valuation is completed and the Valuation Report is received from the bank, the Valuation Report MUST be forwarded to the Real Estate Team so that they are kept informed and updated with the valuation outcome and property details.

Purpose: This information sharing will build an internal reference database that may be used in the future by the Real Estate Team as a reference point in cases of Negative Valuation on similar or nearby properties.

Special Case - No Formal Report Issued: If the bank has only provided the Valuation Amount (a figure/number) without issuing a full formal Valuation Report, then in such cases the Valuation Amount along with the complete Property Details (Building No., Unit No., Building Name, Developer, Area, Emirate, Transaction Type, etc.) must still be compiled and sent to the Real Estate Team.

Applicability: This protocol applies uniformly across all banks, all Emirates (Dubai and Abu Dhabi), and all transaction types (Primary, Resale, Buyout, Equity/Refinance), whenever a valuation outcome (report or amount) is received.

Responsibility: The SPO handling the Valuation Stage for the case (Vijaya, per Section 1.3) is responsible for ensuring the Valuation Report (or Valuation Amount + Property Details, where no report is issued) is shared with the Real Estate Team promptly after receipt from the bank, and that this action is logged/saved in G-Drive along with the rest of the valuation documentation for that case.
Note: This is a newly introduced control point in addition to, and not a replacement for, all existing valuation review and account opening steps described below.

general-valuation-rules-desktop-vs-physi.heading: G. General Valuation Rules, Desktop vs. Physical & Report Scenarios
general-valuation-rules-desktop-vs-physi.h2: SECTION 4: STAGE 2 — Valuation, Inspection & Account Opening SOP

blocks.t: Account Opening: Except DIB bank, we will have to follow-up with the client for account opening in rest all banks.
TAT: After the inspection, 48 Hours is expected TAT for the valuation report from the bank.
Desktop Valuations: Often used for well-established communities, standard apartments/villas, or buyouts with recent records. Faster TAT (24-48 hrs). No physical access needed.
Physical Valuation: Required for luxury, high-value, unique properties, or equity release. Valuer checks condition, size, comparable transactions.
Valuation Scenarios:
Scenario 1 (Valuation = Purchase Price): Bank finances normally based on standard LTV.
Scenario 2 (Valuation > Purchase Price): Bank uses the lower figure (Purchase Price) for financing.

Scenario 3 (Valuation < Purchase Price - Shortfall): Bank finances based on Valuation. Client must cover original down payment + the shortfall difference. Can be challenged with a Bayut report subject to Sir Kiran's confirmation.
Report Check: Check that details on the valuation report are proper (name of the client, address).
Desktop Valuation / Existing Property: Bank will ask for bank evaluation on existing home finance to check if the finance amount against the current market value is less than 60%.

FOL Conversion Details: While valuation is ongoing, SPO sends FOL conversion to VRM mentioning required details based on bank policy. VRM confirms client details (finance amount, tenor, ROI, EMI, life/property insurance) and sends FOL request back to SPO with client confirmation snapshot.
Follow-up: After 2 days ask for update. If delay >3 working days, escalate. Yash (SPO TL) sends pending cases list to banks daily.

blocks.t: Pre-FOL, Post-FOL & Loan Booking Procedural Details:

1. Pre-FOL: While in the valuation stage, once the inspection is completed, SPO needs to send the FOL conversion with the Team Virtue. Once the valuation amount is received, Team Virtue shares the FOL Conversion with SPO. SPO checks the FOL conversion with bank rates, verifies details, and shares them with the bank. Client confirmation on the FOL Conversion is mandatory before sending it to the bank. Usually, most banks take 3-4 days for FOL. During the valuation stage, the client needs to open a Bank Account (except DIB) and keep the account funded as per the required bank amount.

2. Post-FOL: Once the FOL is received, recheck the FOL details: Name of client (Co-Applicant/Borrower if any), ROI, Tenor, Finance Amount, Credit conditions, property address, LTV, etc. If the FOL details are correct, ask the client for FOL signing with a co-applicant or co-borrower (if any). Simultaneously, ask the client to apply for the Liability Letter if required (Seller Mortgage case and Buyout).

3. Loan Booking & Disbursal: Once FOL signing is done, the next procedure is DDA (Direct Debit Authority) activation and Loan Booking. The DDA authorizes the bank to automatically deduct the monthly EMI. In cash seller cases, the file goes directly for the Cleaning Process; meanwhile, SPO takes the DDA Activation confirmation. In buyout and seller mortgage cases, SPO shares the liability letter and informs the bank for loan booking and settlement. Once settlement is done, SPO waits for the Mortgage Release letter, and then the case moves to the Final Transfer stage. Disbursal is the actual release of funds to seller, developer, or existing bank.

blocks.t: Liability Letter: Issued by seller's mortgage bank stating outstanding loan. Valid 5-10 days depending on bank. Name must match MOU/ID. For buyer buyout, only original liability needed.

HSBC Liability Letter Rule: Ask seller to apply via mobile app/online banking. If addressed to Mashreq/DLD and carries the digital line at the bottom ("issued digital"), no wet sign needed. If no line, seller must visit branch for wet stamp. For DLD, select "Courts and government agencies" and type "Dubai Land Department".
Cheque Settlement Workflow:
1. Bank prepares MC to Seller's Bank. If finance amount < outstanding, buyer prepares MC to financing bank.
2. Coordinate appointment with Bank PRO, Real Estate, and Seller.
3. On scheduled day, get confirmation from RE/Seller/PRO that settlement is done.
4. Next day, email bank requesting Settlement Cheque Copy.

Brokerage Clarification Rule: If clearance letter is already attested, ADCB broker is NOT required. Only SCB needed.

Updated SOA / BCC / Handover Notice: For primary transactions. Once FOL received, request Updated SOA for Disbursal. SOA must be valid at handover. blocks.t: Transfer Process Flows by Transaction Type:
Resale Transaction: Manager's Cheques Issuance -> Transfer Appointment -> Existing Mortgage Settlement -> Ownership Transfer -> New Mortgage Registration -> New Title Deed Issuance.
Buyout plus equity: Existing Mortgage Settlement -> Mortgage Release -> New Mortgage Registration -> Updated Title Deed -> Equity Disbursement -> Transaction Completion.
Primary Handover Transaction: Payment to Developer -> Title Deed Issuance -> Property Handover -> Transaction Completion.
Important Dubai vs Abu Dhabi Process Differences:
Dubai transactions are generally processed through DLD Trustee Offices.
Abu Dhabi transactions are processed through ADM or ADGM, depending on the property location.

For a Primary transaction, after the loan is booked, the bank will issue the manager's cheque to the developer. Upon receipt of the payment, the developer will initiate the process of issuing the Title Deed.

blocks.t: A Manager's Cheque is a guarantee cheque issued by the bank by blocking available funds from a current or savings account. It bears authorized bank personnel's signatures. Think of it as: Customer's Money + Bank Guarantee = Manager's Cheque.

"Please prepare the Manager's Cheque amount to the seller AED - [Amount]/- Under the name of - [Seller's Full Name].

(Managers cheque is a guarantee cheque issued by the bank by blocking your available fund from current or savings account. This cheque is different to normal cheque which you issue, you sign. Managers cheque is a cheque which will be issued by the respective bank in which you are having the saving in UAE and the cheque will have the bank authorized person signatures).

operational-scenarios-fund-flow-logic-al.heading: 6.7 Operational Scenarios & Fund Flow Logic (All Transaction Types)
operational-scenarios-fund-flow-logic-al.h2: SECTION 6: STAGE 4 — Final Transfer & Disbursal SOP

blocks.t: Scenario A: Resale / Cash Seller
With Bank Funded Account: Property 1M, Bank Finance 800K, Buyer funded 200K in account. Bank prepares MC of 1M under Seller's Name.
Without Funded Account: Buyer didn't fund self-contribution. Bank prepares MC of 800K under Seller. Buyer prepares separate MC of 200K under Seller.
Scenario B: Resale / Seller Has Mortgage (Liability)

With Bank Funded Account: Property 1M, Bank Finance 800K, Seller Liability 600K. Buyer funds 200K. Bank prepares MC of 1M. At transfer, Bank settles Seller's 600K liability directly to Seller's Bank. Remaining 400K MC given to Seller.
Without Funded Account: Buyer doesn't fund. Bank prepares MC of 800K + Buyer prepares 200K. Bank settles 600K to Seller's Bank, remaining 200K to Seller.
Scenario C: Pure Buyout or Equity Release

Standard: Valuation 1M, Finance 600K, Liability 600K. Bank prepares MC of 600K to settle liability at Seller's previous bank. If extra equity, bank credits remaining funds to client's account post-transfer.
RAK Bank Note: Equity release of AED 500K in customer accounts has been stopped. However, payments can be made directly to contractors.
Scenario D: Direct from Developer

Bank Cheque Calculation: Bank prepares MC based on SOA. If SPA 1M, Finance 800K, SOA Balance 800K, Bank prepares MC 800K to Developer. If SOA Balance 900K, Buyer funds 100K to account, Bank prepares MC 900K to Developer.
Scenario E: Extra Finance Scenarios (Resale Cash & Mortgage Seller)
Note: When buyer wants extra finance, bank covers transfer fees and RE commissions (without VAT) based on LTV.

Resale Cash Seller: If MOU 1M, Finance 800K, Buyer funds self-contribution + Extra Finance/Associated Fees, Bank prepares MC for Total Amount (MOU + Transfer Fee + RE Commission). If Buyer didn't fund, Buyer prepares difference for charges, Bank prepares what it covers.

Resale Mortgage Seller: Same logic, but Bank settles Seller's liability first, then gives remaining balance to Seller. Difference amount for Transfer Fees/RE Commission either covered by Bank (if account funded) or separate MC by Buyer.
ADIB Specific: Gives extra finance to seller directly (no MC to DLD/ADM/RE).

blocks.t: Strict adherence to the G-Drive protocol is mandatory for traceability and upcoming AI/RPA (Robot) integration:
1. Folder Creation (VRM): Open G:\My Drive\Mortgage Department\SALES PROGRESSION OFFICER\2024 CLIENT FOLDER\ON GOING CASES\ -> Create Folder named DD-MM-YYYY / Client and Bank Name.

2. Document Naming & Robot Compliance: Every file must be a separate PDF with a proper heading including the expiry date (e.g., Kiran - Old Passport - Exp 24-05-2024). Documents must be reduced in size before saving. No sub-folders needed if naming is strict.
3. Handover: VRM emails SPO stating documents are saved in G-Drive with the exact file path. SPO picks up, moves, and deletes the created folder.
4. Post-Submission (SPO): Rename main folder to Client Name (Bank). Create sub-folders: Pre-Approval, Valuation, FOL, Loan Booking, Final Transfer.

5. Query Documents: VRM creates a dated folder. Once SPO emails the bank, SPO moves docs to the respective stage folder and deletes the dated folder. Ensure no created folders remain before logging off daily.
